key_insight: LLM agents often solve decomposition benchmarks correctly, but checking the objective alone can miss violations of the prescribed algorithm.
engineering_relevance: Reliable AI-built optimization solvers need execution tests, feasibility checks, method audits, and feedback that pinpoints implementation errors.
method: DecompGym covers 81 instances across five Benders decomposition and four column-generation problem families.
Acceptance requires execution within 60 seconds, numerical feasibility, an LLM-based method audit, and an objective within 1% of the stored optimum.
Evaluate 12 models with up to ten attempts, comparing independent regeneration against failure-diagnosing reflection.
evidence_signal: Two models solved all instances on the first attempt; reflection converted 66% of retries into successes versus 39% for regeneration, while output-only checks would accept 93 of 108 method-audit failures.
watch_item: Method compliance is assessed by an LLM judge rather than formal verification, so audit reliability remains an implementation concern.
paper_title: DecompGym: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Designing Decomposition Algorithms
